newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma sentences opposition MP to four years jail.
newsitem.headline: Burma sentences opposition MP to four years jail.

text.p: Burma's military government has sentenced an elected member of parliament for the opposition National League for Democracy (NLD) party to four years in prison, NLD sources said on Sunday.

NLD chairman Aung Shwe told Reuters Than Aung, a medical doctor, was sentenced at Insein Central Jail on Friday to four years under Section 304(A) of the Penal Code for homicide not amounting to murder.
Than Aung was arrested in February after a patient he gave an injection to later died.
Than Aung was elected as a member of parliament in May 1990 elections that the NLD, which is led by Nobel Peace laureate Aung San Suu Kyi, won by a landslide.
The ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) never recognised the results of the poll and later imprisoned or threatened many of the elected NLD representatives.
Another NLD official said the party had not yet decided whether it would appeal the sentence, although appeals were usually made in such situations.
